title: fix(approval): authorized and review-bot edits to a linked external PR body stale locked issue approvals
body:
## Reproducer

A locked issue approval went stale only because the body of its linked external PR was edited after signing. The maintainer then had to run a second `sudo aidevops approve` for the same issue.

Sequence on #37991 / PR #37992 (external fork PR by a non-collaborator):

1. 01:53:02Z: signed issue approval (comment `6841459828`, `snapshot_sha256` `679aaff2…`). `approve verify issue 37991` returned `proven-locked-continuity` / `VERIFIED`.
2. 01:58Z: maintainer pushed a repair commit to the fork branch.
3. 01:59:46Z: the maintainer edited the PR body to describe the repair (`userContentEdits` editor `marcusquinn`).
4. 02:01:57Z: CodeRabbit rewrote its auto-generated summary block in the PR body (`userContentEdits` editor `coderabbitai`). CodeRabbit does this after every new commit, so step 2 alone would have triggered it.
5. `approve verify issue 37991 --require-authority` then returned `APPROVAL_REASON: stale-or-unproven-continuity` / `STALE_APPROVAL`. `pre-merge-gate` asked for `sudo aidevops approve batch issue:37991`, which made 3 sudo approvals in total for one fix.

Proof: rebuild the current `source-state-unbound` snapshot, substitute the signed lifecycle (as continuity does), and replace only `linked_references[source.number==37992].source.body` with the PR body revision live at signing time (the 01:30:39Z `userContentEdits` entry). That candidate reproduces the signed digest `679aaff2…` exactly. Nothing else drifted.

## Cause

- `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` `_approval_snapshot_v2_linked_source_content` (around lines 219-238): a linked source not authored by an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR of the target repo stays `content_bound: true` and binds its `title` and `body`. That is correct for scope injection by an external author.
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh` `_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity` (around lines 362-375) and `_approval_continuity_content_changes` (around lines 260-275) can only prove that the *issue's own* title/body changed and authenticate those edits (GH#33097 via `_approval_continuity_body_edits_authorized`, lines 283-327). A linked source whose body changed, even by a write-authorized maintainer, puts the frame digest out of range, so continuity fails.

Two edit sources routinely hit this for every external PR repaired after its issue was approved:

- write-authorized maintainers editing the PR body (repair notes, `Resolves`/`For` linkage, verification sections; review policy asks for these)
- review bots that regenerate a delimited block in the PR body (CodeRabbit `<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->` … `<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->`)

## Proposed fix

Extend locked-issue continuity to authenticate linked-source content changes, mirroring GH#33097:

1. In continuity, when the candidate digest differs, also allow a candidate where each content-bound `linked_references[].source` title/body is replaced by its revision at `issued_at`, and the frame then matches. Equivalently, add per-linked-source content digests to new payloads (as `issue.content_digests` does), so the verifier can name which source changed.
2. For each changed source, read its GraphQL `userContentEdits` (issue or pullRequest node). Accept only if every edit at or after the approval anchor has an editor that `_approval_continuity_actor_authorized` returns 0 for (live admin/maintain/write `User`). Treat missing history, a second page, ghost editors or GraphQL errors as uncertainty (return 2), like `_approval_continuity_body_edits_authorized`.
3. For review-bot edits: accept a bot editor only when the before/after bodies differ solely inside a recognised review-bot marker block (start with CodeRabbit's markers). Any byte change outside the block, or an unrecognised bot, stays stale. Keep this allowlist next to the existing review-bot identity config, not inline.
4. Edits by the external source author (or any non-write user) after signing must still stale the approval (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).

Alternative to evaluate (and reject or adopt with rationale in the PR): at merge time, skip linked-source content binding for a source that is itself the PR under merge **and** carries a current exact-head V2 PR approval, since the PR approval already binds that body. This does not cover worker dispatch reads of the issue, so prefer the edit-authentication design above.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/configs/review-bot-body-blocks.conf`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md`

Notes:

- `approval-helper-continuity.sh`: continuity candidate plus linked-source edit authentication.
- `approval-snapshot-v2.sh`: optional per-source content digests in new payloads. Old payloads must keep verifying on exact match.
- Tests: the existing approval continuity tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` (path not fixed; find them with `rg -l "_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity|proven-locked-continuity" .agents/scripts/tests`). Add cases for maintainer edit → VERIFIED, CodeRabbit block-only edit → VERIFIED, external author edit → STALE, bot edit outside its block → STALE, GraphQL uncertainty → API_ERROR.
- `reference/auto-merge.md`: add one line on linked-source edits to the approval continuity section.
- Scope recovery (worker): Proposed fix step 3 requires the review-bot block allowlist next to `configs/trusted-code-quality-bots.txt`, so `configs/review-bot-body-blocks.conf` is added; the test file is the one named in the Tests note.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on changed scripts; the continuity test files pass.
- Replay the #37991 evidence: with the fix, `approval-helper.sh verify issue 37991 marcusquinn/aidevops` against the first signature (comment `6841459828`) and a PR body edited only by `marcusquinn` + `coderabbitai` should return `VERIFIED`. The PR is merged now, so use a fixture built from the recorded snapshot rather than the live issue.
- Pre-existing payload profiles (`trusted-sources`, `stable`, `legacy`) keep exact-match behaviour.

## Related

- GH#32455 (same-repo collaborator sources unbound), GH#33097 (authorized issue title/body edits), GH#34266 (linked-source state unbound). This issue fills the remaining gap: authorized and bot edits to an *external* linked source's body.
- Companion issue on the single-batch approval flow: #38007.

title: fix(review): external PR repair should end in one batch approval, and pre-merge-gate must print it despite a PR needs-maintainer-review label
body:
## Reproducer

Repairing one external fork PR (#37992 for issue #37991) cost the maintainer three `sudo aidevops approve` prompts. The framework design calls for one: `workflows/review.md` "External PR authority preflight" says to finish all approval-bound repairs, then run `pre-merge-gate` and give its single `approve batch issue:N pr:N` command.

1. **Issue approval at review time.** `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` (around line 262) says: "For an issue with an imperfect linked PR, recommend issue approval … then record a separate PR disposition: `merge`, `repair`, `replace`, or `close`." The review therefore ended with `sudo aidevops approve issue 37991 …` even though its own PR disposition was REPAIR. Repairing an external PR always changes the PR head and body, and CodeRabbit regenerates its summary after every push. Under current snapshot binding that stales the issue approval (root cause and continuity fix: #38006).
2. **PR approval only.** After the repair, `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 37992 marcusquinn/aidevops` printed:
   ```text
   [SUCCESS] Review bot gate: PASS — safe to merge PR #37992
   [ERROR] Merge blocked: PR #37992 still requires maintainer review
   ```
   It printed no approval command. The agent hand-built `sudo aidevops approve pr 37992 …` from an earlier issue verification. By then that verification was outdated, so the command was incomplete.
3. **Issue re-approval.** After the PR approval cleared the PR's `needs-maintainer-review` label, the preflight reached authority collection and printed `sudo aidevops approve batch issue:37991 marcusquinn/aidevops`.

If step 2 had printed the full batch command and step 1 had been deferred, one prompt would have covered both targets: `sudo aidevops approve batch issue:37991 pr:37992 marcusquinn/aidevops`.

## Cause

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh` `_merge_pr_label_holds_clear` (around lines 324-329) returns 1 on a live PR `needs-maintainer-review` label. `_merge_collect_external_authority_gaps` (around line 427) calls it before collecting any issue/PR approval targets. That is correct for merge transports (`#aidevops:trust-boundary` GH#17671/GH#28622), but the read-only preflight (`_full_loop_report_external_authority_preflight` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`, around lines 617-656) inherits the hard stop. So it never prints the batch command while the PR's own approval is missing. GH#34568 fixed the sibling path, where the *check* failure stopped the preflight (`diagnostic_only=1` lets a linked-issue NMR become a target), but not the PR-label path. The success path also calls the preflight without `diagnostic_only`.
- `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` line 262 conflicts with `workflows/review.md` lines 51-64 for external/fork PRs whose disposition is REPAIR or REPLACE.

## Proposed fix

1. **Preflight collects everything.** In advisory mode only, treat a live PR `needs-maintainer-review` label as approval target `pr:N` (`approve pr` clears that label) and continue collecting linked-issue targets. Then print one `sudo aidevops approve batch …` covering every missing target. Merge transports (`_merge_guard_admin_merge_maintainer_review`, `cmd_merge`) keep the unconditional hold. `hold-for-review` and the Cloudron release guard stay hard stops in every mode. Decide whether `_full_loop_report_external_authority_preflight` on the success path should pass `diagnostic_only=1`, or a new `advisory=1` flag that does not change Cloudron read-only semantics; document the choice.
2. **Review workflow defers issue approval for repaired external PRs.** Amend `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` around line 262: when the linked PR is external/fork and the disposition is REPAIR or REPLACE (or any approval-bound PR edit is planned), withhold the issue approval command. Record the disposition and give the single post-repair `pre-merge-gate` batch command instead. Issue approval stays immediate when the disposition is MERGE or CLOSE, or when there is no linked PR. The "Maintainer approval" template section should name this case.
3. **Agents never hand-build an approval command for an external PR.** Add one line to `workflows/review.md` "External PR authority preflight": if the preflight prints no command but reports a hold, fix the preflight rather than composing a partial command.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/review.md`

Notes:

- `full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh`: `_merge_pr_label_holds_clear` advisory mode and target collection.
- `full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`: `_full_loop_report_external_authority_preflight` call sites.
- Tests: the existing GH#34568 preflight tests (path not fixed; find with `rg -l "34568|has missing cryptographic development authority" .agents/scripts/tests`). Add a case: external PR carries `needs-maintainer-review` and its linked issue lacks approval → preflight prints `approve batch issue:N pr:N`; merge transport still blocked.
- `review-issue-pr.md`: around line 262 and the "Maintainer approval" template section.
- `review.md`: the External PR authority preflight section.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on changed scripts; the GH#34568 preflight tests and new case pass.
- Manual: on any open external PR carrying `needs-maintainer-review` whose linked issue is unapproved, `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate <PR> <repo>` prints exactly one `sudo aidevops approve batch issue:<N> pr:<PR> <repo>` and `full-loop-helper.sh merge` remains blocked.
- `markdownlint` on the edited workflow docs.

title: fix(pulse): collaborator pulses disarm auto-merge on valid protected release PRs
body:
## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-13
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** During the v3.39.186 release, protected release PR #38003 stalled: auto-merge was enabled by the release lane, then disabled about 2 minutes later by a collaborator account's pulse. The same happened on release PR #37977 (two different collaborator accounts). `aidevops release reconcile` recovered both, but each stall costs a manual reconcile.

## What

Stop collaborator (non-releasing) pulses from disarming native auto-merge on a valid protected release PR, so the release lane's exact `--merge --match-head-commit` queue survives until GitHub merges it.

## Why

Evidence (GitHub timeline, `repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/<N>/timeline`):

- #38003: `auto_merge_enabled` by the releasing maintainer 02:19:48Z → `auto_merge_disabled` by collaborator `vladimirdulov` 02:22:05Z → release helper converted to draft (`version-manager-protected-main.sh:505-507`, "preserved as a draft because exact merge queueing was unavailable") → recovered only by manual `aidevops release reconcile`.
- #37977: enabled 00:24:47Z → disabled by `vladimirdulov` 00:29:06Z → re-enabled 00:32:37Z → disabled by `alex-solovyev` 00:34:53Z → merged 00:42:09Z after manual action.
- Both accounts have `write` permission; the only framework writer of `gh pr merge --disable-auto` reachable from pulse is `_stop_external_native_auto_merge` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:1491-1508`).

Every release therefore needs a human-driven reconcile, and the draft fallback can leave a release lane in `remote-publication` with a dead executor.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** trust-boundary code (`#aidevops:trust-boundary` markers on the disarm paths); the fix must keep fail-closed protection against a drifted release head while not treating "this machine lacks local staging evidence" as drift.

## How (Approach)

### Leading hypothesis (verify first)

`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:164-189` (protected release PR hold): when `protected_release_head_matches_staged "$repo_path" "$head_ref" "$head_oid"` fails, `hold_reason` becomes "protected release PR head differs from staged signed commit **or staging evidence is unavailable**", and an armed auto-merge is disarmed. Staging evidence is created locally on the releasing machine; a collaborator's pulse running on another machine likely has no staging evidence and disarms a perfectly valid release PR.

Other callers that can disarm (rule out each with evidence):
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:618-629` — draft or `hold-for-review` (release PR #38003 had neither at 02:22Z; labels were `status:in-review,release,origin:interactive`).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:1660-1694` — `_handle_existing_native_auto_merge`: synchronous-final-gate, head mismatch vs gated head, stale wedge (>300s).

### Implementation Steps

1. Confirm which path fires: reproduce with the existing harnesses `tests/test-pulse-merge-native-auto.sh` / `tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck-auto.sh` style stubs, simulating a release PR whose staging evidence is absent locally but whose head is the signed release commit (verifiable remotely via `refs/aidevops/release-tags/vX.Y.Z` → tag object → release commit, and the provenance marker `<!-- aidevops:release-provenance tag=... tag-object=... release-commit=... -->` in the PR body).
2. Distinguish "evidence unavailable locally" from "head drifted". Preferred options (pick with evidence):
   - a) Verify the release head remotely (signed tag ref + provenance marker + exact head equality) when local staging is absent; only disarm on proven mismatch.
   - b) Make non-releasing pulses skip protected release PRs entirely (no merge attempt, no disarm) when local staging is absent; the releasing machine's lane/reconcile owns them.
3. Keep fail-closed behavior for a proven head mismatch (head ≠ signed release commit) — that remains a disarm.
4. Ensure `_handle_existing_native_auto_merge` stale-wedge and head-mismatch paths do not disarm a release lane's `--match-head-commit` request whose head still equals the signed release commit.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:164-189` — protected release hold decision.
- `EDIT (if implicated): .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:1660-1694`.
- `READ: .agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh:455-513` — release lane queue/draft fallback contract.
- `READ: protected_release_head_matches_staged` (locate with `rg -n "protected_release_head_matches_staged" .agents/scripts`).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Trust boundary: never allow a drifted/forged head to merge. Remote verification must bind tag ref, tag object, release commit and PR head exactly.
- Mixed-version fleet: collaborators run older pulses until they update; the release lane's draft fallback + `aidevops release reconcile` remains the recovery path.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-native-auto.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck-auto.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh` pass.
- ShellCheck clean on modified files.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-native-auto.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified with evidence (which function disarmed #38003/#37977 on a non-releasing machine).
- [ ] A pulse lacking local staging evidence no longer disarms auto-merge on a protected release PR whose head equals the remotely verifiable signed release commit.
- [ ] A protected release PR whose head differs from the signed release commit is still disarmed (fail closed).
- [ ] Existing pulse-merge tests and ShellCheck pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Release recovery today: `aidevops release reconcile <source-PR>` re-queues the exact merge; it worked for both incidents.
- Collaborator pulse logs are not accessible from the releasing machine; the hypothesis is based on code paths and timing, not log lines.

title: feat(cloudron): routine-bump standing policy for commit-tracked and main-build upstreams
body:
## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-13
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Standing release policies were created for all eight Cloudron package repos. Three (librecrawl, opendesk, buzz) can never satisfy the routine-bump predicate because their `upstreamVersion` is not strict `X.Y.Z`. The maintainer asked for those policies anyway plus a task to make them effective.

## What

Extend the standing-policy routine-bump predicate so packages whose upstream is tracked by commit (`upstream_source: commits`) or by a main-build suffix can qualify as routine upstream bumps, with an equivalently strict, fail-closed proof.

Affected repos (policy issues already created, awaiting signature):
- `marcusquinn/cloudron-librecrawl-app` #60 — `upstreamVersion` `789c236` (commit SHA prefix).
- `marcusquinn/cloudron-opendesk-app` #107 — `upstreamVersion` `7a47f44` (commit SHA prefix).
- `marcusquinn/cloudron-buzz-app` #131 — `upstreamVersion` `0.5.28-main.2cd40ba` (semver + main build suffix), while its monitor findings are titled `Buzz upstream v0.5.27 is available` (tag-based).

## Why

`.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py:35-36,69-73,183-192` requires `upstreamVersion` to fullmatch `v?X.Y.Z` and the finding fingerprint to be `upstream-vX.Y.Z` (`.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:341-344` requires `fingerprint == upstream-v*`). Commit-mode findings (`.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh:665-672`, issues titled `LibreCrawl upstream commit 789c236 is available`) never match, so every bump of these repos needs a per-release signature even with a signed policy.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** trust-boundary predicate that authorizes unsigned publication; commit SHAs have no ordering, so "upstream must increase" and "same major" need a different, sound proof.

## How (Approach)

### Implementation Steps

1. Read how commit-mode findings are fingerprinted and what they prove: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh` (commit source ~lines 660-770, including the qualified release-parent image proof at ~765) and `release_upstream_finding` in `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` (locate with `rg -n "release_upstream_finding" .agents/scripts`).
2. Commit mode: accept `upstreamVersion` as a hex SHA prefix (≥7) when the policy/repo declares commit mode, require it to equal the open trusted finding's commit, and prove forward progress with the GitHub compare API (`repos/{upstream}/compare/{old}...{new}` status `ahead`) instead of tuple ordering. Decide (and document) whether commit bumps have any "major" boundary; default: no major boundary, but keep all other predicate rules (patch-only package bump, file allowlist, substitution-only edits).
3. Buzz-style `X.Y.Z-main.<sha>`: determine whether the package should pin a tag (`X.Y.Z`) to match its tag-based findings, or whether the predicate should accept the suffix form bound to the finding. Prefer fixing the package convention if the monitor finding is tag-based; otherwise extend the regex with an exact bound to the finding.
4. Policy schema: if the predicate needs to know the mode, add an explicit field (e.g. `upstream_mode: "commits"`) to `release_policy_body` (`.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:248-256`). Note: changing the policy body changes what a maintainer signs — existing signed policies must keep verifying (default mode = semver); new modes need a fresh policy body + signature.
5. Pinned-file substitution (`substitute_versions`, `cloudron_routine_bump.py:99-107`) must handle SHA tokens (whole-token, no partial-prefix matches).

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` (finding fingerprint acceptance ~341-344; policy body ~248-256 if schema changes)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` (routine predicate cases ~819-900 are the reference pattern)
- `READ: .agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Trust boundary: a commit finding must be bound to the exact upstream repo and SHA; a non-fast-forward (diverged/rewritten) upstream must fail closed.
- Existing signed policies (aidevops-cloudron-app #271, netbird #242, headscale #59, nostr-relay #40, warmbly #34, orbit #13) must remain `VERIFIED` and keep semver semantics.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` passes, with new predicate cases for commit mode (accept forward SHA; reject diverged, mismatched finding, partial SHA token substitution).
- ShellCheck clean; `python3 -m py_compile .agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A librecrawl/opendesk-style routine bump (patch package bump, `upstreamVersion` old SHA → new SHA equal to the open trusted commit finding, upstream compare `ahead`) returns `ROUTINE_BUMP`.
- [ ] Diverged/behind upstream SHAs, mismatched findings, or non-allowlisted edits are rejected.
- [ ] Buzz has a documented, working path (package convention change or predicate support) to routine bumps.
- [ ] Existing semver policies keep verifying and keep their current predicate behavior.
- [ ] Tests and ShellCheck pass.

title: fix(dispatch): expired prelaunch checkpoint claim is never released, stranding the maintainer approval
body:
## What

An approval-bound checkpoint continuation claim that expires at `phase=prelaunch` is never released. Nothing retries it either. The maintainer's approval is stranded, and `approval-template` refuses a fresh one. Close this gap automatically, without needing the claim owner's manual `abort-pr-checkpoint-claim`.

## Reproducer

Observed once in production; no synthetic reproducer yet. Managed private repo; runner v3.39.184; maintainer host v3.39.186.

Issue timeline for `<repo>#<issue>` / draft `#<pr>`:

1. 00:34Z: maintainer publishes `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` (exact head; `runner` = runner B, the runner of the released attempt).
2. 00:35Z: `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION … stalls=6` (fuse reached). The approval owns scheduling for 24 h.
3. 00:38Z: runner B posts `DISPATCH_CLAIM … phase=prelaunch checkpoint_mode=revision checkpoint_approval=<approval id> max_age_s=1800`.
4. After that: no `DISPATCH_LEASE`, no "Dispatching worker" notice, no `CLAIM_RELEASED`. The issue is unassigned with `status:available`. Three hours later runner B's pulse is active on other issues but has not retried this one.
5. Maintainer `approval-template <repo> <pr> <issue> <release> attempt:<id>` → `intervening coordination is not fully released; no approval generated; rejected comment=<claim> event=DISPATCH_CLAIM runner=<B> episode_claim=<claim> reason=open_at_end`.

Why it stays stuck:

- The automatic orphan release in `dispatch-claim-helper.sh:684-716` → `_post_orphan_claim_release` (`:775`) only posts when the claim author equals the current runner (`:789`). It runs only inside that runner's own claim path, and runner B never re-enters that path for this issue.
- The documented fallback (`reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` "Expired claims that never reached ready (GH#35331)") requires the claim owner to run `abort-pr-checkpoint-claim` by hand on their host. For a cross-operator fleet, that is a human round trip per occurrence.
- Related but distinct: GH#37735 (assigned/in-progress strand after a launch failure before prelaunch) and GH#37669 (`worker_not_launched` reuse).

## How (choose with evidence; keep the existing trust model)

- **Preferred:** each runner's pulse sweeps its **own** expired `phase=prelaunch` checkpoint claims. These have no ready lease, no launch notice and no release, and their expiry is known and elapsed. The sweep posts the existing `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=claim_only_no_worker` through `_post_orphan_claim_release` with the same device/session revalidation as `_dch_orphan_release_valid`. Bound it per cycle. Candidate entry point: the stalled-checkpoint / `dispatch-stalled` cadence in the pulse.
- Then `approval-template` already accepts the `claim_only_no_worker` successor (GH#35331 path), so the maintainer can re-approve. Alternatively, the approval can be reused automatically, as the GH#37669 `worker_not_launched` path does, because the head did not change.
- Also find why the 00:38Z attempt died after the claim without a release. Capture the stage from runner B's attempt log if it is reachable, or add a release on that exit path.

## Acceptance

title: fix(checkpoint): dispatch-approved silently ignores a valid approval when an older approval names another PR
body:
## What

`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-approved` silently never launches a valid approval when the issue history also has an older approval for a **different** PR (or runner). Discovery requires exactly one distinct `{pr, runner}` pair across all trusted, unedited approvals. An issue whose first draft merged and whose second draft was later approved can therefore never resume.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-approved <repo> <path> <issue> <login>; echo "rc=$?"` on an issue with approvals for two different PRs.

**Actual output:** no output, `rc=1`, and the attempt log is 0 bytes. **Expected:** the newest valid approval is dispatched.

Code: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:863-882` (`_pcc_dispatch_approved`):

```jq
[... select(startswith("CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED ")) | ... | {pr,runner}] | unique |
select(length == 1) | .[0] | [.pr,.runner] | @tsv
```

Observed (managed private repo, v3.39.186):

- Issue `<issue>` has two unedited approvals: 11-10 for draft A (since **merged**), and 11-12T19:33Z for draft B (open, exact head unchanged).
- `approval-template` for draft B today regenerates the identical approval line, so the approval is valid.
- Pulse calls `dispatch-approved` every cycle (`pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh:426-446`). Every attempt log `worker-pr-checkpoint-continuation-<repo>-<issue>.log.*` is **0 bytes**: the jq `-e` fails, the function returns 1, and nothing is logged.
- After more than 8 h, no runner had claimed draft B. Pulse keeps logging `stale_draft_checkpoint … rearm_blocked=fleet_window_pending:86400s` for the issue.

## How

- In `_pcc_dispatch_approved`, choose the **newest** trusted, unedited approval for this repo/issue, ordered by comment `created_at` and then `id`, instead of requiring a single distinct pair. `_pcc_dispatch` already re-verifies the full envelope (exact head, brief SHA, release history and claim consensus), so discovery does not need to fail closed on history.
- Optionally restrict candidates to approvals whose `pr` is still an open draft before choosing the newest.
- When discovery finds approvals but returns none, log one line naming the reason (for example `approval_discovery=ambiguous pairs=N`) to the attempt log. That way 0-byte logs no longer hide the refusal.

## Acceptance

- An issue with an older approval for a merged or closed PR and a newer valid approval for the open draft dispatches the newer one.
- Refusals in discovery leave a one-line reason in the attempt log.

## Verification

- Add a case next to the existing dispatch-approved tests (`rg -l 'dispatch-approved' .agents/scripts/tests`): two approvals for different PRs, where the newest is selected.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`

### Files Scope

- EDIT: the matching test under `.agents/scripts/tests/`
- EDIT (if behaviour is documented): `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

title: fix(pulse): draft checkpoint strands consolidated specs without auto-dispatch; attention comment reposts under App reads
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Task

Two defects keep a `consolidated` spec waiting for a person after a worker stops at a draft checkpoint.

1. The checkpoint removes `auto-dispatch` from the issue and nothing puts it back. A consolidated spec is only a dispatch candidate while it carries that label, so no later pass continues its draft PR.
2. The comment that reports this is meant to be posted once per draft PR head. On a repository that Pulse reads through a GitHub App installation, each runner posts it again every six hours.

Restore the label at the step that returns the issue to the queue, when this same worker run removed it. Make the comment's duplicate check recognise write-access authors when GitHub does not report them as members.

**Done when:** a worker draft checkpoint on a canonical consolidated spec leaves the issue `status:available` with `auto-dispatch`, unless a hold label or an assignee is present; a label that a person removed before the checkpoint stays removed; and the attention comment is not posted again for a head that already has one from an account with write access.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/37888/timeline --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.event == "labeled" or .event == "unlabeled" or .event == "assigned" or .event == "unassigned") | "\(.created_at) \(.actor.login) \(.event) \(.label.name // .assignee.login)"'`

**Actual output:** read at 2026-11-13T03:25Z, seven lines from one worker run (the runner login is the worker's):

```text
2026-11-12T09:07:02Z <runner> labeled status:in-progress
2026-11-12T09:13:58Z <runner> unlabeled auto-dispatch
2026-11-12T09:14:05Z <runner> unlabeled status:in-progress
2026-11-12T09:14:08Z <runner> labeled status:in-review
2026-11-12T09:15:22Z <runner> unassigned <runner>
2026-11-12T09:15:26Z <runner> unlabeled status:in-review
2026-11-12T09:15:28Z <runner> labeled status:available
```

The issue then stayed `status:available`, unassigned, `consolidated`, without `auto-dispatch`, with draft PR #37889 open, for 18 hours. Each pass logged `consolidated management-label gate skipped #37888 (blocked:consolidated would always reject; GH#35038)`.

**Expected:** the last step also restores `auto-dispatch`, and the next pass continues the draft.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief</summary>

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `consolidated auto-dispatch draft checkpoint stranded attention` and `author_association CONTRIBUTOR installation token private org member` → no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` on the four target files → no open PR and no claimed issue. Related and not covering this: GH#35038 (added the enumeration filter and the attention comment), GH#37043 (restores `auto-dispatch` on stranded available issues, and refuses while any PR is open), GH#37600 (treats a canonical spec without the label as an owner hold), GH#24546 and GH#34644 (private organization members reported as `CONTRIBUTOR` or `NONE`).
- [x] File refs verified at `main` `26499e452b` on 2026-11-13: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh` `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint`:286-330; `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_project_post_release_state`:971, draft-checkpoint branch :993-1011; `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` `_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch`:534-582; `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` `_dispatch_consolidated_checkpoint_attention`:1544-1593; `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority`:40-123; `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh` `_has_consolidated_label`:490-508.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — both causes are located and the design below is settled
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped; implemented in the session that wrote this brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-13, ai-interactive, from a maintainer-requested review of why queued work waits for an interactive session
- **Evidence window:** public issue timelines and comments read on 2026-11-13; comment counts on a managed organization repository; a read-only report from a session with access to two worker hosts

## What

1. Draft-checkpoint release: restore `auto-dispatch` on a canonical consolidated spec when the escalation in the same worker run removed it.
2. Attention comment: count an existing comment for the same draft PR head as present when its author has write access, resolved through the shared permission helper.

## Why

- **Where the label is lost.** `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint` moves the issue to `status:in-review` and removes `auto-dispatch` (`headless-runtime-worker-output.sh`:294, :307). It then releases the claim. For reason `worker_draft_checkpoint`, `_hrff_project_post_release_state` (`headless-runtime-failure.sh`:993-1011) unassigns the runner, sets `status:available` and calls `_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch`, which refuses while any PR is open (`pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`:571). A draft checkpoint always has an open PR, so the label stays off.
- **Why only consolidated specs strand.** An ordinary `status:available` issue is a candidate without `auto-dispatch` (`pulse-repo-meta.sh`:607-610), and dispatch then continues its draft head. `_has_consolidated_label` accepts a consolidated issue only with `auto-dispatch` and the canonical `_Supersedes #N — this issue is the consolidated spec._` line, so the enumeration filter drops the spec on every pass.
- **Measured.** On 2026-11-13 three open specs across the managed repositories were in this state for 18 hours, 11 hours and 5.5 days; two were `priority:high`. One was GH#37888, the spec for the REST quota drain that defers most Pulse stages on the maintainer's runner. The label was re-added by hand at 03:30Z. Exact-head continuation of GH#37888 was dispatched 10 minutes later. The second spec was dispatched after 8 minutes and its PR merged 43 minutes after the label came back. A worker took the third after 27 minutes.
- **Why the comment repeats.** The duplicate check accepts a comment only when `author_association` is `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`:1563-1565). A session on the worker hosts reported that the same comment reads as `MEMBER` through the runner's own login and as `CONTRIBUTOR` through the App installation token that Pulse reads use there. All three memberships of that organization are private. Each runner therefore treats the existing comments, its own included, as untrusted and posts again when its six-hour stamp expires. One issue has 44 copies for one head from three accounts (1, 21 and 22); another had 5. On GH#37888 the same code posted once in 18 hours; its author reads as `COLLABORATOR`.
- **Scope of the repeat.** In the newest 3,000 comments of that repository (14 hours), this is the only keyed HTML marker posted more than twice with an identical key. Other `author_association` filters were not examined; a separate issue covers them.

## Tier

`tier:standard`. Four small edits with one trust decision, described below.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh` — `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint` (:286): before the transition, for the draft-checkpoint reason only, record whether the issue is a canonical consolidated spec that carries `auto-dispatch`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` — new guarded restore beside `_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch` (:534)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` — draft-checkpoint branch (:993-1011): call the new restore after the existing one
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` — new helper: does any comment that contains a key come from an account with write authority
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` — duplicate check in `_dispatch_consolidated_checkpoint_attention` (:1562-1567) calls that helper; this file is 1,959 lines, so keep the edit to a few lines
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh` — attention duplicate check cases
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` — restore cases

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint` is called from `headless-runtime-worker.sh` (five sites) and `headless-runtime-failure.sh` (one); only the draft-checkpoint reason reaches the changed branch. `_dispatch_filter_consolidated_candidates` is the only caller of the attention helper. `auto-dispatch` on a consolidated issue is read by `_has_consolidated_label` at enumeration and inside `dispatch_with_dedup`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** one added label write per draft checkpoint on a canonical consolidated spec, through `set_issue_status`. No new comment: the `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_draft_checkpoint` comment and the label timeline record the step. The attention helper posts fewer comments, never more.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A — `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` reuses the existing attention limits and TTL.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the five scripts are copied to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` by `setup.sh`; no generated output.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A — `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` acts only on a checkpoint taken after deployment. Specs stranded earlier keep the attention comment; three were repaired by hand.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the commit; `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` stores nothing, and a restored label stays valid under the older code.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint`, when the release reason is the draft checkpoint, read the issue once before the transition. If it is open, labelled `consolidated` and `auto-dispatch`, and its body has the canonical marker line, set a process-local receipt naming the repository and issue. A failed read sets nothing.
2. Add `_pmpc_restore_checkpoint_spec_dispatch <repo> <issue>`. It returns without writing unless the receipt names this issue. It then reads the issue again and requires: open, not a pull request, no assignee, `status:available` as the only status label, `consolidated`, the canonical marker, and none of `auto-dispatch`, `no-auto-dispatch`, `parent-task`, `hold-for-review`, `lockdown`, `persistent` or any `needs-*` label. It adds `auto-dispatch` through `set_issue_status` and logs one line. Mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
3. Call it from the draft-checkpoint branch after `_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch`, best-effort.
4. Add a helper to `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` that takes a repository, comments JSON and a key. It lists the distinct authors of comments whose body contains the key and returns 0 when any of them passes `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority <repo> <login> <association>`, 1 when there is no such comment or every author is confirmed without write access, and 2 when a lookup failed and none passed.
5. In the attention helper, call it in place of the association test: 0 records the head as already reported, 1 posts as now, 2 skips the post for this TTL. Keep the association test as the fallback when the helper is not loaded.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** GH#37600 treats a canonical spec without `auto-dispatch` as an owner hold. The restore undoes only the removal made by the same worker run, proven by a read taken before that removal. A label removed by a person before the checkpoint is absent at that read, so no receipt exists. A hold added during the release is seen by the second read.
- **Competing branch:** the label was removed so that no second worker opens a new branch while the draft exists. After the restore, `dispatch_with_dedup` still finds the draft and routes the exact head; this was observed on GH#37888 after the manual repair.
- **Duplicate check:** a comment from an account without write access must not suppress the notice. The permission helper returns trusted only for `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or a write-or-higher permission, and unknown on lookup failure.
- **API cost:** one issue read per draft checkpoint; one permission read per distinct non-member author of a matching comment, per stranded issue per TTL.
- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the receipt is process-local to the worker run. Adding a present label is a no-op.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored state or format changes, so there is nothing to migrate; reverting the commit restores today's behaviour and leaves restored labels in place.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an older runner still strands specs and still reposts; a newer runner does neither. No shared state changes format.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the receipt is cleared on use. A second call writes nothing.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the label write fails, the issue is in the state it is in today and the attention comment reports it.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the consolidated-label test covers the duplicate check; the partial-continuation test covers the restore guard; the two runtime tests show the escalation and release paths still behave; `shellcheck` covers the edited scripts.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — four scripts and their tests.

### Scope Boundaries

- Do not change `_has_consolidated_label` or let a consolidated issue dispatch without `auto-dispatch`.
- Do not restore the label from timeline or comment evidence; only from the same-run receipt.
- Do not change `_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch` or its open-PR refusal.
- Do not change other `author_association` filters here.
- Do not delete the duplicate comments already posted.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a worker draft checkpoint on a canonical consolidated spec that carried `auto-dispatch`, the issue is `status:available` with `auto-dispatch`.
- [ ] A spec whose `auto-dispatch` was absent before the checkpoint is not relabelled.
- [ ] An issue with `no-auto-dispatch`, `hold-for-review`, `parent-task`, `lockdown`, `persistent`, a `needs-*` label, an assignee or a status other than `status:available` is not relabelled.
- [ ] An issue that is not a canonical consolidated spec is not relabelled.
- [ ] A matching comment whose author reads as `CONTRIBUTOR` and has write permission suppresses a repeat post.
- [ ] A matching comment whose author has no write permission does not suppress the post.
- [ ] A failed permission lookup posts nothing in that pass.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh` — checkpoint escalation that removes the label
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` — release projection that returns the issue to the queue
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` — existing guarded restore, and home of the new one
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` — enumeration filter and attention comment
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` — permission helper (context only)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh` — the gate that needs the label (context only)

</details>

title: perf(pulse): first-wave round-robin census starves the product repo holding the backlog — 20-slot runner idles at 1-2 workers
body:
## Observed

A 20-slot runner with 70 pulse-enabled repositories ran at `workers=1/20` and `workers=2/20` for about an hour (2026-11-13 03:40–04:40 UTC). The one product repository that held almost all launchable work had 19+ clean candidates, with `auto-dispatch`, `status:available`, no assignee, no linked PR and no blockers. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <N>` on one of them reported no backoff, no progress blockers and no prior attempts.

Pulse log evidence (deployed v3.39.187):

```text
Dispatch_max: available=20, candidates=88            # wave A: census reached the product repo
Dispatch_max stopping early: cooperative drain requested for activated bundle 3.39.187-... (GH#37907)
Dispatch path=max complete: implementation_dispatched=3 ... processed=8/88
...
Post-label dispatch_max skipped: insufficient wall-clock budget (remaining=0s, required=1182s)
...
candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=202s
Dispatch_max: available=18, candidates=2             # wave B: started after the cursor, product repo not scanned
...
Minimum worker floor refill: active=2/6, attempt=1/6 — re-enumerating candidates
candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=301s
Dispatch_max: available=19, candidates=1             # floor refill: product repo not scanned again
Dispatch_max: skipping #3 (...) — cross-cycle block:worker_draft_checkpoint_cooldown
Minimum worker floor refill stopped: dispatch_max returned 0
...
Post-label dispatch_max skipped: insufficient wall-clock budget (remaining=0s, required=1050s)
pulse-health.json written: workers=1/20
```

`~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-first-wave-cursor` had moved to repository index 42 of 70. The product repository is index 4.

## Root cause

1. **The first-wave census is a plain round-robin over repositories.** `_dispatch_repository_rows` (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) rotates `repos.json` order from `pulse-first-wave-cursor`. `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json` stops once the 180 s `PULSE_FIRST_WAVE_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_S` deadline passes and it has any candidate. `_dispatch_first_wave_advance_cursor` moves the cursor past every polled repository. With 70 repositories at about 3–15 s each, one wave covers about 20–40 of them. A product repository with a deep backlog is therefore scanned roughly one wave in three. Meanwhile a tooling repository with one blocked candidate ends each wave and keeps the slots empty.
2. **The floor refill re-enumerates in first-wave mode.** It does not continue down the ranked list from the earlier wave (#37874 step 4). The wave-A list of 88 candidates was dropped after the cooperative drain stopped it at 8/88. Wave B and the floor refill then re-ran the rotating census from the cursor.
3. **The full (post-label) census never runs.** Early dispatch plus the merge pass use the whole cycle budget (`preflight_early_dispatch` took 1717–3164 s), so `Post-label dispatch_max skipped: insufficient wall-clock budget` repeats. Only the first-wave rotation feeds launches.

## Proposed fix

- Weight the first-wave scan order by evidence of launchable backlog instead of plain rotation. For example, scan first the repositories whose last complete census produced candidates that were never attempted (or `priority:product` repositories with non-empty last-census candidates), then rotate the rest. This keeps the GH#33647 fairness for empty or blocked repositories without starving the deep one.
- When a cooperative drain or budget stop interrupts a wave, persist its unattempted ranked remainder (with a census-duration TTL, as in #37874 step 4). The next wave or floor refill then resumes it before it re-enumerates from the cursor.
- Optional: count "first wave ended with fewer candidates than free slots while a known non-empty repository was skipped" as a stat, so this starvation shows in `pulse-health.json`.

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — `_dispatch_repository_rows`, `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json`, `_dispatch_first_wave_enumeration_done` (first-wave order and stop rule).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` — `_dispatch_ranked_candidates_json` snapshot reuse across waves and the floor refill.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` — floor refill path (`Minimum worker floor refill`), reusing the ranked remainder.
- Tests: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`. Use the existing fixture style with 70 repositories, where one product repository holds 20 fresh candidates and another holds 1 blocked candidate. Assert that the product repository is scanned in every first wave until its candidates are attempted.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`

Integration evidence: early dispatch and bounded refill explicitly disable snapshots in pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh and pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh; both callers must enable the separate partial-census cache. Existing first-wave and candidate-snapshot suites plus ShellCheck verify this integration.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` and `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh` pass. ShellCheck must report zero issues.

title: fix(pulse-merge): review-decision refresh is REST-only and deferred at worker reserve, stalling all green-PR merges
body:
## Problem

The deterministic merge pass stops merging every green collaborator PR when REST core quota drops below the worker reserve. When the prefetched `reviewDecision` is empty, which GitHub returns for repos that do not require a review, `_pmp_normalize_review_decision_into` maps it to `UNKNOWN`. The only refresh path is `_pmp_rest_review_decision_from_reviews` → `_pmp_rest_reviews_json`. That function calls `gh_budget_worker_reserve_allows` before each page and returns 1 at or below the 20% reserve. The PR is then skipped with `reviewDecision unavailable after refresh (GH#26218)`.

So merges, which are pulse priority 1 and shrink the backlog, get deferred as optional REST work. GraphQL budget is still available when this happens.

## Evidence (supervisor pulse, 2026-11-13T04:17Z)

- `gh api rate_limit`: core 478/5000 remaining (reset 05:09Z), graphql 4673/5000 remaining.
- The pulse log has 106 `reviewDecision unavailable after refresh` skips. The latest merge pass skipped about 20 green, `MergeState: CLEAN` worker PRs in a managed product repo and 6 PRs in this repo, for example #38019, #38015, #38000, #37983, #37960 and #37768.
- `gh pr view <N> --json reviewDecision` returns `""` for an affected product-repo PR with `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. That is a no-required-review state, not missing evidence.
- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N> --verbose` shows only the GH#26218 skip line after `no terminal failed required contexts`.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-rest-state.sh`: `_pmp_refresh_unknown_review_decision_into` (~L242), `_pmp_rest_review_decision_from_reviews` (~L215) and `_pmp_rest_reviews_json` (~L180).
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-budget-policy.sh` (`gh_budget_worker_reserve_allows`), only if you choose to treat merge-gate review reads as priority work instead of optional work.

## Suggested approach (pick the smallest safe option)

1. When REST is at reserve, fall back to one bounded GraphQL read, `gh pr view N --repo SLUG --json latestReviews,reviewDecision`. Derive the state with the same semantics as the REST jq: each author's latest state-changing review; any `CHANGES_REQUESTED` → `CHANGES_REQUESTED`; any `APPROVED` → `OBSERVED_APPROVED`; else `NONE`. Malformed data still fails closed (`UNKNOWN`).
2. Alternatively, classify this single-page review read as merge-priority work so the worker reserve does not apply to it. Keep the hard REST floor.

Do not treat `""` as `NONE` without reading reviews. The GH#26218 intent is to never miss a CHANGES_REQUESTED review.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-rest-review-decision.sh` passes. Extend it only if it already stubs the reserve gate: assert that REST at reserve still resolves the review state through the fallback, and that malformed GraphQL output yields `UNKNOWN`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-rest-state.sh` reports zero violations.
- After deploy, during a low-REST window, the pulse log shows `Merge pass` merges instead of GH#26218 skips for CLEAN green PRs.

## Related

- #37888 / PR #37889: same-login REST-core drain attribution. That is the cause of the low quota; this issue is about how the merge pass degrades when quota is low.

## What

Pulse cannot start a CI repair for a pull request whose head commit is not already in the runner's local object store. The repair worktree step fetches the PR branch with a plain `git fetch` against the canonical checkout, and the canonical Git guard denies every `git fetch` there (exit 42). The lease records the failure as a remote-access problem, and the PR then waits for a person.

## Why it matters

A PR pushed by another runner or device, or advanced on the remote (for example by a merge of the default branch), is exactly the case where the head is not held locally. Those PRs get no automatic repair from this runner after their required checks fail. Pulse logs `retryable in-place repair launch failure ... preserving PR for a later bounded attempt` each cycle and nothing changes. Worker PRs were observed open for two to seven hours with terminal failed required checks and no repair attempt that reached a worker.

## Evidence

- On one runner, 7 of the 10 CI-repair leases written in 48 hours ended with `status=worktree_failed stage=head_fetch failure_reason=pr_head_fetch_failed next_action=verify_remote_branch_access_and_retry`. The 3 that reached `dispatched` were PRs whose head commit was already local.
- The only producer of `pr_head_fetch_failed` in the repair path is `_ci_repair_create_worktree` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh`:
  `git -C "$repo_path" fetch --no-tags --quiet origin "$pr_head_ref" >/dev/null 2>&1`
- Policy probe (no Git command runs): `canonical-git-command-guard.py --cwd / --argv-json '["-C","<canonical-checkout>","fetch","--no-tags","--quiet","origin","<branch>"]'` exits 42 with `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git fetch'`. `cat-file` and `ls-remote` on the same target exit 0.
- Pulse runs with the framework `git` shim first on `PATH`, so the guard applies to this call.
- For the failed leases the remote branch existed and the remote is public HTTPS, so remote access was not the cause.
- stderr of the fetch is discarded, so the guard message never reaches a log.

## Reproducer

1. On a runner whose `PATH` puts the framework `git` shim first, pick an open same-repository PR whose head commit is not in the local object store (`git -C <canonical-checkout> cat-file -e <head-sha>^{commit}` fails) and whose required checks have a terminal failure.
2. Let the merge pass route it to the CI fix-worker.
3. Observed: `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker: retryable in-place repair launch failure ... (result=retryable)`, and the lease `state.json` holds `stage=head_fetch failure_reason=pr_head_fetch_failed`. No worktree, no worker.
4. Expected: a repair worktree at the exact PR head and a dispatched repair worker.

The guard decision reproduces without a network call or a repository change:

```bash
python3 .agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py --cwd / \
  --argv-json '["-C","<canonical-checkout>","fetch","--no-tags","--quiet","origin","<branch>"]'
# exit 42: BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git fetch'
```

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing-cases.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing-mocks.sh`

The function to change is `_ci_repair_create_worktree`. The mocks file changes only if the fixture needs it.

Reference pattern: `_prrts_fetch_exact_worker_head` in `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`. It fetches from a linked-worktree context: an existing sibling worktree of the repository when one is present, otherwise an owned, locked scratch worktree from `scratch_worktree_add` in `.agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh` (GH#35024), removed afterwards with `scratch_worktree_remove`. Refspec: `+refs/heads/<head_ref>:refs/remotes/origin/<head_ref>`.

Steps:

1. When the exact head commit is missing locally, fetch the PR branch from a linked-worktree context as above instead of from the canonical checkout.
2. Keep the existing exact-SHA `cat-file` verification after the fetch and keep `--base "$pr_head_sha"` for the repair worktree, so a branch that moved is still reported as `pr_head_commit_unavailable` / `worktree_head_mismatch` with `refresh_pr_head_and_retry`.
3. Give the "no fetch context could be created" case its own diagnostic reason, and make `next_action` for a failed fetch name the real next step. Do not print the discarded stderr of an authenticated command into a public log; a bounded reason is enough.
4. Do not weaken the canonical Git guard and do not bypass the `git` shim.

## Acceptance

- With a `git` on `PATH` that refuses `fetch` when the target is the canonical checkout (as the guard does) and a PR head that is absent locally but present on the remote, `_ci_repair_create_worktree` returns a worktree whose `HEAD` equals the PR head.
- With the head already local, behaviour is unchanged and no fetch context is created.
- A scratch fetch context created by the function is removed on success and on failure.
- A branch whose remote tip differs from the expected head still fails closed with the existing reasons.
